title.narrative: Enhancing the wellbeing of the Karantina community through improved urban farming skills and practices

description.narrative:
The urban farming project, planned to be implemented in the historically disadvantaged neighbourhood of Karantina in Beirut, is designed to tackle the intertwined challenges of food insecurity and socio-economic hardship faced by vulnerable communities, including Lebanese hosts, internally displaced persons (IDPs), refugees, and migrants.
The project will directly benefit 200 vulnerable individuals, primarily women and youth, from both Lebanese and refugee backgrounds. An inclusive approach will be adopted that prioritize women-headed households, large families, the elderly, individuals with special needs, and unemployed youth, aiming to identify those most at risk. This participatory project design is supported by key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs) to engage the community in planning and ensure the project aligns with their needs.
The project seeks to equip vulnerable groups in Karantina with improved agro-food skills and practices and to increase food security and wellbeing within targeted households through greater agricultural productivity and income generation.
The first objective focuses on building urban farming and agro-food skills, fostering a foundation of knowledge and expertise among women and youth to enable them to support their households more effectively. Outreach campaigns will introduce beneficiaries to the project, outlining selection criteria and activities, while a community center will host the training sessions. Accessible land will be secured in the targeted neighbourhood to provide a practical environment for agricultural skills application, where participants can develop their farming and food processing capabilities. These sessions will empower women and youth to engage directly in urban farming activities. The training ensures beneficiaries can confidently produce, market, and sell high-quality, homemade food items, helping alleviate household food insecurity.
The second objective is to improve food security and overall wellbeing for households through increased food production and income generation. Once trained, beneficiaries will apply urban farming techniques within their homes or local community spaces, supported by toolkits tailored for home farming and food processing. Regular site visits will provide technical guidance, helping trainees troubleshoot any issues and maintain high standards for quality control and food storage. Additional training sessions will explore advanced agro-food methods to enhance product life and maximize yields from various vegetables.
The project’s ongoing support will further strengthen food security and wellbeing, as participants leverage their skills and resources for personal consumption and income generation. Follow-up visits will monitor the impact of these activities on household wellbeing, while community kitchens will continue to serve as hubs where women and youth can refine their urban farming skills. In this way, the project will not only deliver immediate socio-economic benefits but also will foster long-term empowerment and resilience for Karantina’s most vulnerable groups.
